column1: # relative-json-pointer acceptance vectors, from
# draft-handrews-relative-json-pointer, the draft the validator implements.
# relative-json-pointer = non-negative-integer ( "#" / json-pointer ), so the
# pointer half is RFC 6901's production verbatim. The official suite's
# optional/format/relative-json-pointer.json carries 18 cases covering the
# integer prefix, the leading-zero ban, and a bare "#". It reaches none of the
# RFC 6901 escape rule the pointer half inherits, nothing following the "#", and
# neither form of the later draft's index manipulation.
# Row format: see loadVectorFile in vectors_test.go.

column3: a multi-digit prefix without a leading zero

column1: 2/highly/nested/objects

column3: the index form after a non-zero prefix

column1: # The RFC 6901 escape rule the pointer half inherits.

column3: ~0 escapes a tilde in the member name
~1 escapes a solidus in the member name

column1: 0/a%2Fb
column3: %2F is an ordinary member-name character, since RFC 6901 spells a solidus ~1 (cfea10e, 9dd7528)

column1: # The '#' terminates the pointer; nothing follows it.

column3: a pointer cannot follow the index form

column1: 1#foo
column3: text cannot follow the index form

column1: 0foo
column3: the prefix must be followed by '#' or a pointer

column1: # The index-manipulation production. draft-bhutton-relative-json-pointer-00
# §3 adds ( "+" / "-" ) non-negative-integer between the prefix and the
# pointer; draft-handrews, which this validator implements and which both
# supported drafts of the specification cite, has no such production.

column3: index manipulation belongs to the later draft
index manipulation belongs to the later draft
